Subject: Request: scan cadence, SLA & CVE recovery commitments for SOC2 review

Hi Kimberly,

We're preparing for FinPoint's vendor SOC2 readiness review and need to collect explicit commitments from critical vendors. For Redwood we need the following items by EOD Thursday: 

- Current vulnerability scanning cadence (internal infra + 3rd-party deps) and the primary tooling used.
- SLA for remediation windows by CVE severity (e.g., critical/urgent/high/medium).
- Proof of recent scan results (single PDF snapshot is fine) and an example CVE remediation ticket showing timeline from detection to closure.
- Confirmation whether you commit to a 30/60/90-day closure SLA (we categorize by criticality).

Can you also confirm an owner we can reach during our audit window (next week)? If possible, include a short written statement we can attach to our SOC2 binder.

Thanks,
Asha Menon
Security & Vendor Risk
FinPoint Capital

--

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you've requested; summary below and attached artifacts in the Drive link. See the attached snapshot (scan_snapshot_20270520.pdf) and a CSV of recent CVE tickets.

Quick summary (for inclusion in your SOC2 binder):
- Scan cadence: Weekly authenticated host scans for prod and staging (Nessus), daily container image scanning (Trivy + internal SBOM checks), dependency SCA on push with Snyk (policy gate on high/critical).
- CVE remediation SLAs (Redwood standard):
  - Critical (RCE privilege escalation with exploitability): 7 calendar days for remediation or documented compensating control; 72-hour escalation to SRE on-call.
  - High (remote code execution without public exploit): 30 calendar days
  - Medium: 90 calendar days
  - Low: tracked and reviewed quarterly
- Escalation & rollback policy: automatic on-call page for P1/P0; can trigger hotpatch windows or temporary isolation of service until fix validated.
- Owner for audit/review: Rishi Malhotra (Security Engineering) — rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, +1-555-0192.

Attached artifacts (also uploaded to the Drive folder): scan_snapshot_20270520.pdf, cve_action_plan_FP-4512.xlsx (sample remediation plan + timeline), and a redacted ticket export showing detection->patch->verify for CVE-2027-1054.

If you need a signed letter for the binder we can produce one tomorrow on Redwood letterhead.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Asha — adding technical detail to Kimberly's summary for your SOC2 notes and to satisfy auditor questions.

1) Detection & verification workflow (short):
- Automated findings feed: Trivy/Snyk/Nessus -> internal triage queue in Jira security-project (tagged REDWOOD-SCAN).
- Triage SLA: findings triaged within 24 hours; critical findings receive immediate assignment.
- Proof-of-fix: patch PR + CI green + deploy + post-deploy authenticated re-scan to confirm remediation; evidence saved in the ticket.

2) Example timeline (redacted ticket included):
- 2027-05-12 02:14 UTC: automated scan detected package libsigma v2.3.1 with CVE-2027-1054 (high).
- 2027-05-13 09:08 UTC: triage completed, assignment to service owner.
- 2027-05-20 03:35 UTC: patch PR merged; canary deploy initiated.
- 2027-05-20 10:11 UTC: post-deploy re-scan shows vulnerability cleared; ticket closed 2027-05-20 15:02 UTC.

3) Compensating controls: for any case where immediate remediation would cause unacceptable risk, we document temporary mitigations (network ACLs, rate-limits, additional monitoring) and set a window for the permanent fix. Those appear in the cve_action_plan_FP-4512.xlsx.

4) Audit artifacts we will share (redacted where necessary): latest authenticated host scan snapshot, pipeline SCA run logs for the last 30 days, a redacted ticket export for one closed CVE (above), and an architecture note showing isolation controls.

If the auditor needs a confirmation signature we can provide Rishi's signed technical statement and Kimberly's higher-level attestation.

Rishi
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
